messages:
Jamie: hey all — first week, trying to wire up a streaming demo. quick q: how are rate-limit buckets configured for hosted API keys vs sandbox? i'm hitting 429s when I open ~8 concurrent streams. is that per-connection, per-token, or per-route?
Alex: welcome! short answer: sandbox has much lower shared quotas. hosted (org) keys get larger buckets depending on plan. 429s are usually from concurrency or tokens/min buckets, not "per-connection" alone.
Sara: tl;dr there are a few buckets to think about: requests/sec (concurrency), tokens/min, and active streaming connections. sandbox defaults are intentionally small (example: ~5 req/s, ~4 concurrent streams, 5k tokens/min) to protect shared infra.
Miguel: when you get a 429, inspect the response headers — we expose remaining and retry info. example:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 1678900000
x-rw-retry-after: 1.2
content-type: application/json
{ "error": "rate_limited", "message":"exceeded tokens/min" }
```
Alex: note the headers vary slightly between hosted vs sandbox but the pattern is the same. Hosted may give larger windows and different reset math.
Liz: for streaming demos, avoid spinning up N separate connections. reuse a single streaming session when possible or multiplex requests over one connection. For retries use exponential backoff + jitter. simple pseudocode: 
```
backoff = base * 2**attempt + random(0, base)
// base ~ 500ms, cap ~ 5s
```
Sara: also remember token accounting: streaming still counts tokens as they are generated/consumed. if your demo sends long prompts repeatedly you'll burn the tokens/min bucket fast. batching or caching prompts helps.
Jamie: got it — do I need to request quota increases somewhere for sandbox or hosted?
Alex: for sandbox — file a request in #devex with your email and project name and we can bump you temporarily. For hosted/prod you need an account admin to request via Console -> Account -> Quotas or contact sales/CS depending on org.
Miguel: FYI: there's a lightweight self-serve boost for new hires that devex can enable (tmp for 48h). OncallBot: devex-boost-request created (ID: DBR-421) — devex will follow up.
Jamie: thanks — last Q: do embeddings calls count against the same tokens/min bucket or separate?
Sara: embeddings usually count toward tokens/min too but some workload tiers have separate embedding buckets. check the per-route headers; if you see separate x-rw-embed-... headers then it's segregated. otherwise assume shared.
Liz: if you want, DM me your demo scenario and I can suggest config changes (batch sizes, prompt trimming) to avoid hitting 429s. :thumbsup:
Jamie: awesome, thanks everyone! I'll open a devex thread and try multiplexing first. :raised_hands:
